description:
From the fz-kdt.198 cold review (2026-09-03). Under 198's encoding a Descr is
ONE rectangle S x B (kind union x brand slot). union is the pointwise HULL:
exact when the operands agree on one factor (Meters | int = int; Meters |
Feet), but ANY union whose operands disagree on BOTH factors releases the
slot to ⊤ and loses the brand entirely: `@spec take(utf8 | nil)` and
`@spec take(utf8 | integer)` accept a bare binary on interp, run and build
(probe/p1_union_nil.fz, p3_union_int.fz), and still do with fz-kdt.192's
raw-argument gate stacked. TypeExpr::Union (resolve.rs:278-286) is the
language's ONLY type combinator, so the encoding cannot carry a brand
through the one operator specs are written with. A missed diagnostic, never
a miscompile (brands are erased before the backend), and strictly smaller
than HEAD's inverted order -- which is why 198 lands with this as a labelled
known-wrong pin (HEAD accepts the same program). THE FIX (data-model up):
the brand slot moves DOWN onto the per-axis DNF clauses (a union of
rectangles), where clause order / absorption / idempotence already exist;
union then keeps (utf8, binary) and (unbranded, nil) as two clauses; intersect
and diff distribute over clauses; canon renders each clause's refinement.
BLOCKS: trusting a brand at a @spec gate (fz-kdt.201's return side, any
brand-typed argument gate beyond the single-brand case), and the owner's
minting form once it exists. Red-first: p1_union_nil / p3_union_int reject
the bare binary on three doors; the residue pin flips from known-wrong to
law. CONCORDANCE: fz-kdt.198 (the rectangle encoding this extends), fz-
kdt.182/48 (DNF normalisation and denotational identity -- the same clause
machinery), fz-kdt.172 (DNF hygiene coverage), fz-kdt.201, fz-kdt.192.
title: A union with a different-kind operand loses the brand: the brand slot is per-DESCRIPTOR, so `utf8 | nil` admits a bare binary -- the descriptor must hold a union of rectangles (the slot on each DNF clause) before a brand can be trusted at a @spec gate
